name: Alignment Quotient
measurement_target: Judge-rated adherence of a response to the stated goal and constraints of the prompt
observable: Properties of the response text relative to the visible prompt, as rated by an LLM judge; the user's actual (hidden) intent is NOT observed
instrument: LLM-as-judge, rubric fingerprint SCORING_PROMPT_HASH, 0-100 sub-scores combined by fixed weights

goal_clarity.observes: how precisely the response addresses the visible goal, as judged

constraint_aware.observes: respect of explicit and inferable constraints, as judged

path_coherence.observes: whether the reasoning path leads to the conclusion, as judged

scope_drift.observes: staying within scope (100 = perfectly scoped), as judged

reality_grounding.observes: grounding of claims in verifiable reality, as judged — NOT verified against the world

theory_inspiration: Instruction-following evaluation literature (inspiration only, not an implementation): AQ does not decompose instructions into atomic checkable requirements — that is the planned PIGA direction
allowed_claims: Response X tracks its visible prompt's goal better than response Y, as judged, under configuration Z
prohibited_claims: The system is aligned (with anyone): AQ observes one response against one visible prompt, not values, intent reconstruction, or behavior under distribution shift
Prompt-intent alignment: the human's actual intent is not part of the observation
Cross-configuration comparisons of absolute AQ values (MAD 12.7)
known_confounds: A response can track a MISREAD goal coherently and score well (goal misidentification is invisible without ground-truth intent)
Judge-relative scale; documented LLM-judge biases (verbosity, position, self-preference)
statistics: mean over n samples; Bessel-corrected SD; Student-t CI at n>=2; no significance claims at current sample sizes

validity_evidence.content: rubric facets map to goal/constraints/scope; no expert panel yet
validity_evidence.reliability: Run 001 H2 as for all dimensions

validity_domain: English single- and few-turn interactions with a visible prompt; nothing established about hidden-intent alignment
